findings.title: A backup code can log in without the password when any totpCode is also sent
findings.body:
The password check at line 121 is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is truthy. The new backup-code branch at line 131 takes precedence over the TOTP branch and never looks at `totpCode`. A direct POST to the NextAuth credentials callback with `email`, `backupCode` and any non-empty `totpCode` (for example `000000`) therefore authenticates with only a backup code. No password is checked and no TOTP is verified. The UI never sends both, but the endpoint accepts it.

The backup code is a replacement for the TOTP code, not for the password. It is also only 40 bits of entropy (10 hex characters). Skipping the password check on that path weakens the login more than the TOTP-only path already does.

Fix: in the backup-code branch, require that `totpCode` is empty. For example, only take the branch when `credentials.backupCode && !credentials.totpCode`. Alternatively, make the password check at line 121 run whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves 2FA enabled but the UI and modal state stale
findings.body:
After `TwoFactorAuthAPI.enable` succeeds (line 134), 2FA is already enabled server-side. The only handlers that reset the step and call `onEnable()` are the Close button (lines 266-270) and the wizard's own Cancel button, which is hidden on this step (line 222). The Dialog's `onOpenChange` (Esc, overlay click, X) is passed straight to the parent. In `apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64` it only toggles `enableModalOpen`. The parent's `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()` runs only in `onEnable` (lines 65-68).

Two things go wrong after such a dismissal:
- The settings page keeps showing the switch as off although 2FA is on, until a reload.
- The modal component stays mounted with `step === DisplayBackupCodes`. Reopening it shows the old backup codes instead of the password step, and `resetState` is never called.

Fix: handle dismissal inside the modal. Wrap `onOpenChange` so that on the backup-codes step it also runs `resetState()` and `onEnable()`. Alternatively, block dismissal on that step.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code reads the encrypted list, nulls one entry and writes back the whole list. Two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass the `indexOf` check, so a single-use code is used twice. Two concurrent logins with different codes can overwrite each other's write, which restores a code that was already used. Consider a conditional update, for example `updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: <old ciphertext> }` and a check that `count === 1`. Consider a transaction as an alternative.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode throws an unhandled 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` throws a TypeError when the JSON body carries a non-string truthy value such as `123` or `{}`. The route has no try/catch, so the request fails with an unhandled 500 instead of a 400 `IncorrectBackupCode`. Check `typeof req.body.backupCode === "string"` first. The same routine failures (the missing key at line 51, a bad decrypt or JSON.parse at line 58) throw instead of returning an error code, which the modal then shows as a generic 'something went wrong'.

findings.title: Component is named TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export is called `TwoFactor`, the same name as `components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx`. It shows up under the wrong name in React devtools and stack traces and invites mix-ups when auto-importing. Rename it to `BackupCode`. The input also has no `autoFocus`, so the user has to click into it after pressing 'Lost access'.

findings.title: resetState leaves backup codes in memory and the blob URL unrevoked
findings.body: `resetState` clears the password, the error and the step, but `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `secret` and `dataUri` stay in component state. The object URL created at line 99 is revoked only when a later setup runs (line 98), never on close or unmount, so a Blob holding the plaintext codes lives until the page is closed. Revoke the URL and clear the state in `resetState`. Also type the state, since `useState([])` infers `never[]`: `useState<string[]>([])`.

findings.title: Backup-code login and disable paths have no tests
findings.body: The new server logic is untested: login with a backup code, single-use consumption, a wrong code, disabling with a backup code, and the `backupCodes: null` clear on disable. The only added coverage is the download, copy and close buttons on the enable flow. Both the TODO at line 12 and the FIXME at line 50 describe known gaps in the PR itself. At minimum, add an e2e or unit test that logs in with a backup code and checks that a second use of the same code fails.

contracts.action: Login with a backup code (new credentials field backupCode)
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing TOTP branch at next-auth-options.ts:157-187 and the password check at :121-129
contracts.before_after: Before: password is verified unless totpCode is present, then the TOTP is verified. After: the backup-code branch runs first and ignores totpCode. If totpCode is present, the password check is skipped and the backup code alone is accepted. Otherwise the password is checked and then the code is matched and consumed with a DB update.
contracts.visible_effect: A valid code logs in. A wrong code surfaces as incorrect_backup_code in login.tsx:157. A missing list surfaces as missing_backup_codes.
contracts.failure_mode: A request with a non-empty totpCode plus a backup code bypasses the password. Concurrent use of the same code is not atomic. A missing CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY throws InternalServerError, which the UI shows as a generic message.

contracts.action: Enable-2FA modal shows backup codes after TOTP verification and closes via Close button
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous behaviour called onEnable() directly at the same point; the parent two-factor-auth.tsx:65-68 closes the modal and invalidates viewer.me
contracts.before_after: Before: the modal closed on success. After: it moves to DisplayBackupCodes, and only the Close button calls resetState and onEnable. Esc, overlay click and X go through onOpenChange, which only toggles the open flag.
contracts.visible_effect: The user sees the codes with copy, download and close. If dismissed another way, the settings switch stays stale and the modal reopens on the codes step.
contracts.failure_mode: Stale parent state and stale modal step after a non-Close dismissal. Reaching this step required successful enable and setup responses; if the setup response lacked backupCodes, `body.backupCodes.map` throws inside try and shows 'something went wrong'.

contracts.action: Disable 2FA with a backup code and clear stored codes
contracts.equivalent_path: TOTP branch in the same file (lines 69-100)
contracts.before_after: The password is verified first in both paths. The backup code is matched against the decrypted list. The code is not consumed, because all codes are nulled on disable at line 107. If the update fails, the code stays valid.
contracts.visible_effect: The modal closes via onDisable on a 200. Error codes are mapped to messages in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:67-76.
contracts.failure_mode: A non-string backupCode causes an unhandled 500. A missing encryption key throws.

contracts.action: Setup endpoint generates and returns 10 backup codes
contracts.equivalent_path: Existing secret generation and storage in the same handler (lines 58, 70)
contracts.before_after: Codes are generated with crypto.randomBytes and stored encrypted with the same key as the secret, with twoFactorEnabled still false. Each repeated setup call regenerates them. A cancelled setup leaves codes and a secret stored while 2FA is off, as the secret already did.
contracts.visible_effect: The codes are shown after TOTP verification, from client state.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. The codes are returned before TOTP is verified, but are only usable once twoFactorEnabled is true.

summary: The backup-code feature is mostly sound, but it has two real defects. First, `next-auth-options.ts` lets a backup code log in without the password if the request also carries any non-empty `totpCode`, because the password check is skipped whenever `totpCode` is present and the backup-code branch ignores `totpCode`. Second, `EnableTwoFactorModal` leaves the settings page stale after Esc, overlay click or X on the backup-codes step. There, 2FA is already enabled, but the parent never gets `onEnable` and the modal reopens on the codes step. Smaller items: a non-atomic backup-code consume, a 500 on a non-string `backupCode` in `disable.ts`, the `BackupCode` component exported under the name `TwoFactor`, backup-code state and the blob URL never cleared, and no tests for backup-code login or disable. I read the changed files and the callers I cite; I did not build or run anything.
